Project Objectives: We propose a unique strategy to protect perovskite solar cells (PSCs) and enhance their lifetime towards reaching SETO’s 2030 cost target of $0.02/kWh. Specifically, this program aims to encapsulate PSCs with transparent conductive composites (TCCs) to isolate them from the external environment. We will use our expertise in semiconductor surface passivation and protection against corrosion gained from years of DOE/EERE- funded research in PEC water-splitting to further develop TCC protection layers (Task 1) and benchmark their effectiveness towards enhancing PSCs durability (Task 2), aiming for less than 10% reduction in efficiency (T90) over 1,300 hours of continuous operation for PSCs with initial PCE greater than 22% (EOP goal). Objectives: Task 1.0: Validation of TCCs as efficient gas-barriers Task Summary: To develop TCCs (conductive media + polymer) with appropriate gas- barrier and optoelectronic properties for the prolonged operation of PSCs, relevant parameters such as WVTR, electrical conductivity, and optical transparency were benchmarked before and after exposure to aging conditions. Subtask 1.1 – Polymers water vapor (WVTR), and oxygen (OTR) transmission rate benchmarking: WVTRs of solvent-free, room-temperature curable polyepoxies were measured using NREL's established techniques before and after 1,000 hours of damp heat (45°C, 85% R.H.) aging. The facilities required for OTR testing were to be established at NREL; however, this was not completed within the project period. Subtask 1.2 – Quantify the effect of aging on TCCs' optoelectronic properties: Polymers were combined with conductive media to form TCCs and exposed to 1,000 hours of outdoor aging to benchmark changes in optical and electrical properties over time. Task 2.0: PSCs durability benchmarking Task Summary: To evaluate process compatibility and optoelectronic performance of monolithically integrated IZO/TCC/PSC devices, photovoltaic (PV) metrics were benchmarked and assessed before and after encapsulation.
